codebook.definition: Threat or action explicitly conditioned on a stated trigger (deal, opening, deadline).
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when 'if X not done, then Y' structure with identifiable X or deadline.

codebook.definition: Escalation threat or intimidation without a defined trigger, target or time.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use for menacing language lacking measurable condition.

codebook.definition: Report of completed or ongoing physical action (strike, interdiction, seizure).
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when specific event is claimed as having occurred.

codebook.definition: Assertion that an agreement exists, is near, or has been approved.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when text says deal done, agreed, imminent or approved, with or without terms.

codebook.definition: Remarks on state, pace, posture or existence of talks.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when talks are described, denied, characterized or used to pressure the counterpart.

codebook.definition: Suspension, postponement, or removal of threatened punitive action.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when strikes, tariffs or blockade steps are paused, cancelled or eased.

codebook.definition: Tariff or trade measure with concrete rate, date, scope or legal step.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when at least one of rate, date, product or procedure is given.

codebook.definition: Tariff talk lacking parameters; complaints, praise or general intent.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when tariffs are discussed without operational detail.

codebook.definition: Statements about Strait of Hormuz passage, blockade, tolls, mines, or oil flow.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use whenever shipping access or oil movement is a main topic.

codebook.definition: Specific terms or conditions of an agreement (nuclear, funds, inspections, signatories).
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when substantive terms are enumerated.

codebook.definition: Attack on media, critics, predecessors or prior deals.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when text rebuts or insults non-counterpart actors.

codebook.definition: Claims of dominance or victory, with unverifiable superlatives.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use for success claims about military or economic state.

codebook.definition: Post that shares or retweets third-party content without own assertion.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use for pure links, headlines or RTs.

codebook.definition: Cites named allies or mediators as source of request, approval or participation.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use when specific leaders are named as part of the action.

codebook.definition: Policy design, doctrine, fee, organisational or strategic goal statement.
codebook.inclusion_rule: Use for non-event announcements of rules, fees, objectives or institutions.

Q001.credibility_cue: Slogan only; no parameters, but event date is real
Q001.memo: Celebratory post on reciprocal tariff day with no rates or details.

Q002.credibility_cue: Specific rate and duration; hedged by "subject to documents"
Q002.memo: Pauses 50% Canada tariffs for three days citing a deal pending documents; floats reviving Keystone XL.

Q003.credibility_cue: Cites Navy briefing; verifiable by shipping data
Q003.memo: Reports Strait mines cleared per Navy and warns new mine-laying will be destroyed.

Q004.credibility_cue: Specific incident, named platform, crew status; response unspecified
Q004.memo: Reports Iran downed a US Apache, pilots safe, and says the US must respond.

Q005.memo: Asks Iranian leaders to release detained women as a goodwill opening to negotiations.

Q006.credibility_cue: Large specific figures; counterpart confirmation absent
Q006.memo: Announces South Korea deal: $350B payment for lower tariffs, energy purchases, $600B investment, submarine approval.

Q007.credibility_cue: Detailed combat claims by president; unverified damage figures
Q007.memo: Claims three destroyers exited Hormuz under fire, destroyed attackers, and warns of harder strikes unless deal signed fast.

Q008.memo: Links article by former economist saying Iran deal boosts US economy.

Q009.memo: Declares Iran will pay many times over for any American death; directive passed to military leaders.

Q010.credibility_cue: Concrete troop number and one-month window; counterpart call cited
Q010.memo: Mexico agrees to send 10,000 troops; tariffs paused one month while named officials negotiate.

Q011.credibility_cue: Admits deal unseen and unfinished; self-vouching
Q011.memo: Defends yet-unseen Iran deal as better than Obama deal and dismisses critics.

Q012.credibility_cue: Specific concessions asserted, contradicted by Iran per own text; escrow mechanics given
Q012.memo: Says Iran agreed to inspections, Strait stays open, blockade lifted unless needed, funds in US-controlled escrow for food purchases.

Q013.memo: Says strongly considering large banking sanctions and tariffs on Russia until ceasefire; urges talks.

Q014.credibility_cue: Mixed claims of agreement with vague trigger; military posture stays
Q014.memo: Forces remain until agreement complied with; threatens renewed strikes if not; says Hormuz will be open and safe.

Q015.credibility_cue: Specific two-week window; conditional on Hormuz opening; mediators named
Q015.memo: Suspends Iran attack for two weeks at Pakistan request, conditional on Strait opening; says deal near and cites 10-point Iranian proposal.

Q016.credibility_cue: Specific exemption scope and end date
Q016.memo: Exempts USMCA-covered Mexican goods from tariffs until April 2 after call with Sheinbaum.

Q017.memo: Retweets article claiming Iran deal means economic boom.

Q018.memo: Says Japan visiting today to negotiate tariffs, military cost and trade fairness; hopes for good outcome.

Q019.credibility_cue: Cancels attack subject to rapid deal; claims Israel joins; terms broad
Q019.memo: Cancels planned attack after Iran request, citing agreed deal parameters including Hormuz opening, conditional on quick deal.

Q020.memo: Says countries want trade deals and predicts growth.

Q021.memo: Claims Iran told US it is in state of collapse and wants Hormuz opened.

Q022.memo: Demands unconditional surrender from Iran, then promises reconstruction and a new leadership.

Q023.memo: Reports Vietnam leader says tariffs would be cut to zero if a deal is made.

Q024.credibility_cue: Specific targets struck; existential threat unspecific
Q024.memo: Reports strikes on Iranian missile, drone and radar sites for ceasefire violation; warns Iran may cease to exist.

Q025.credibility_cue: Specific five-day window and target class; conditional on talks
Q025.memo: Postpones strikes on Iranian power plants and energy infrastructure five days due to productive talks.

Q026.memo: Links article of Iranian opposition figure praising the deal memorandum.

Q027.memo: Says Iran military destroyed, calls Iran all talk, says it will pay the price for slow negotiation.

Q028.credibility_cue: Brief, ties strike to specific prior event
Q028.memo: States strike is retribution for Iran bombing ships; promises worse if repeated.

Q029.credibility_cue: Signing date tomorrow; specific terms; says no money; self-promotional comparison
Q029.memo: Says Iran deal to be signed tomorrow, Hormuz then open, no nuclear weapon, no money exchanged, uranium to be removed later.

Q030.credibility_cue: Relays Iranian claim; conditions stated; fund use specific
Q030.memo: Says Iran denies tolls; talks end if false; US releases Iranian funds only for American farm purchases.

Q031.credibility_cue: Framework only; tariff cancellation dated; negotiators named
Q031.memo: Cancels February 1 tariffs after framework with NATO chief on Greenland and Arctic; negotiators named.

Q032.credibility_cue: Claims Iranian request; condition is Hormuz opening
Q032.memo: Says Iran asked for ceasefire; US will consider once Hormuz open, otherwise continues bombing.

Q033.memo: Links article quoting Trump that deal is imminent and talks restart Monday.

Q034.credibility_cue: Specific threat (power plants, bridges); reveals negotiators travelling; blockade facts
Q034.memo: Accuses Iran of ceasefire violation, sends negotiators to Islamabad, offers a deal, threatens to destroy power plants and bridges otherwise.

Q035.credibility_cue: Contests CNN; cites agreement content unseen
Q035.memo: Rebuts CNN claim that the Iran deal lacks nuclear provisions.

Q036.credibility_cue: Attributes to Iran; shouting caps; "Strait of Iran" wording
Q036.memo: Says Iran announced the Strait is fully open for passage.

Q037.credibility_cue: Many named leaders; "largely negotiated, subject to finalization"
Q037.memo: Reports call with Gulf, Pakistani, Turkish, Egyptian, Jordanian leaders; MOU largely negotiated, Hormuz to be opened, details soon.

Q038.credibility_cue: Exact rate, date and trigger; escalation of prior action
Q038.memo: Threatens extra 50% tariffs on China from April 9 unless 34% retaliation withdrawn by April 8; ends meetings.

Q039.credibility_cue: Names Gulf leaders; attack stands ready on short notice
Q039.memo: Calls off scheduled attack on Iran at Gulf leaders request while ordering readiness for large assault if no deal.

Q040.credibility_cue: Concrete multi-part sanctions with rates and timing

Q041.credibility_cue: Detailed conditional; distances US from Israeli strike
Q041.memo: Distances US from Israeli strike on South Pars; says no more Israeli attacks unless Iran hits Qatar again, then US destroys field.

Q042.credibility_cue: Demand with vague time; references prior strikes
Q042.memo: Tells Iran to stop Lebanese proxies or be hit harder.

Q043.credibility_cue: Claim of strike outcome, no detail

Q044.credibility_cue: 301 probe is concrete step; tariff rate and timing undefined
Q044.memo: Announces Section 301 investigation of EU fines on US tech firms and anticipates substantial tariffs soon.

Q045.credibility_cue: Specific tariff figures; "subject to final approval"
Q045.memo: Says China deal done pending Xi approval: rare earth magnets supplied, students, 55% US tariffs vs 10% for China.

Q046.memo: Denies forcing Iran to negotiate, says indifferent to deal, claims control of Hormuz and Iranian economic collapse.

Q047.memo: Repeat link on Iranian opposition praise for deal.

Q048.memo: Rejects NYT claim goals unmet, says ahead of schedule and Iran wants a deal while he does not.

Q049.memo: Announces many long-sought targets in Iran destroyed.

Q050.credibility_cue: Lists five objectives; shifts Hormuz burden to others
Q050.memo: Lists objectives for winding down Iran operations; says Hormuz must be policed by user nations, not the US.

Q051.memo: Says Iran cannot sign non-nuclear deal and should get smart soon.

Q052.credibility_cue: Detailed day-count of contacts; denies reports
Q052.memo: Denies talks stopped; says conversations continued daily and urges Iran to make a deal.

Q053.credibility_cue: Specific delegation names; call length; scope limited to trade
Q053.memo: Reports 90-minute call with Xi on trade deal and rare earths; teams to meet; no Iran or Russia discussed.

Q054.credibility_cue: Flat denial of talks; contradicts other posts
Q054.memo: States no talks occurring or scheduled with Iran, blockade in force, Hormuz open, mines cleared.

Q055.credibility_cue: Open-ended extension of ceasefire; blockade continues
Q055.memo: Extends ceasefire at Pakistan request pending unified Iranian proposal; blockade continues.

Q056.credibility_cue: Claims total control; unverifiable internal Iran claims
Q056.memo: Says Iran has leadership infighting, US Navy controls Hormuz, sealed until Iran makes a deal.

Q057.memo: Hails day for world peace, says US will help Hormuz traffic, big money, Iranian reconstruction.

Q058.memo: Says nations receiving oil via Hormuz must secure passage with US help.

Q059.memo: Says Canada wants statehood benefits and charges farmers heavy tariffs; "no more".

Q060.credibility_cue: Names the paused program; blockade stays; short vague duration
Q060.memo: Pauses Project Freedom ship escorts through Hormuz for a short time while agreement is finalized; blockade remains.

Q061.credibility_cue: Detailed terms; pending final decision; retweet
Q061.memo: Lists terms: no nuclear weapon, Hormuz open without tolls, blockade lifted, uranium to be destroyed, no money; final decision pending.

Q062.credibility_cue: Calls on named countries; continuing strikes

Q063.memo: Defends Iran attack, attacks Democrats and cites the State of the Union.

Q064.memo: Announces furniture tariff investigation finishing within 50 days; rate to be determined.

Q065.credibility_cue: Specific incident cited; strike under way; further threat unspecified
Q065.memo: Announces strikes near Hormuz in retaliation for mine attempt and missiles at Jordan base; threatens harder strikes.

Q066.memo: Says Iranian negotiators are begging for a deal, warns no turning back.

Q067.memo: Links Breitbart piece of Kurdish leader praising Trump.

Q068.memo: Claims nine Iranian naval ships sunk and naval headquarters largely destroyed.

Q069.credibility_cue: Specific numbers rhetorical; conditioned on assassination threat
Q069.memo: Says 1000 missiles aimed at Iran if it acts on assassination threats; one-year destruction authority.

Q070.credibility_cue: Detailed list of terms; final decision pending
Q070.memo: States Iran must agree no nuclear weapon, open Hormuz, no tolls, clear mines; blockade lifted; uranium destroyed.

Q071.memo: Says no enrichment, uranium removal, tariff and sanctions relief under discussion, many of 15 points agreed.

Q072.memo: Says Iran has no cards except Hormuz extortion; alive only to negotiate.

Q073.memo: Announces creation of External Revenue Service on January 20, 2025 to collect tariffs.

Q074.credibility_cue: Sweeping secondary-sanction threat; no named measures

Q075.memo: Threatens Tuesday attacks on Iranian power plants and bridges unless Strait opened.

Q076.credibility_cue: Specific date and rates; stays scheduled

Q077.credibility_cue: Accuses Iranian duplicity; contrasts public and private
Q077.memo: Says Iran requests talks yet denies them, asserts US Navy blockade controls Hormuz.

Q078.memo: Warns that further Houthi attacks will bring US punishment on Iran and the Houthis.

Q079.credibility_cue: Names targets (power, wells, Kharg); hedged "probably" deal

Q080.memo: Links Bloomberg report of Bessent saying Iran talks include dollar invoicing.

Q081.credibility_cue: Exact rate and date; sooner-if-escalated; export controls
Q081.memo: Announces 100% extra tariff on China and software export controls from November 1 in response to Chinese rare earth controls.

Q082.credibility_cue: Rambling; links oil price to elections
Q082.memo: Accuses Houthis acting for Iran of driving up oil prices before elections; vows to remember.

Q083.credibility_cue: Specific rate; conditional on EU removing whisky tariff
Q083.memo: Threatens 200% tariffs on EU alcohol unless 50% EU whisky tariff removed immediately.

Q084.credibility_cue: Specific counts and drug claim; claims unverifiable
Q084.memo: Says Iran navy of 158 ships destroyed, warns approaching ships will be eliminated, claims drug flows cut.

Q085.credibility_cue: Concrete action; explicit conditional restraint on oil infrastructure
Q085.memo: Announces bombing of military targets on Kharg Island, spares oil infrastructure unless Hormuz passage is disrupted.

Q086.credibility_cue: Principle without rates or dates; instructs agencies
Q086.memo: Announces reciprocal tariff policy matching foreign tariffs and VAT; orders cabinet to implement.

Q087.credibility_cue: Calls on Israel and Hezbollah; peace deal described as close
Q087.memo: Criticizes Israeli Beirut attack, calls for restraint, says close to Iran peace deal.

Q088.memo: Describes Chinese rare earth export controls, cancels Xi meeting prospects, threatens massive tariffs and countermeasures.

Q089.memo: Says unofficial lists and letters on Iran talks are fraud; only US points matter.

Q090.memo: Postpones strikes on Iranian power and energy infrastructure for five days given productive talks.

Q091.credibility_cue: Specific date (November 3); self-limiting commitment; oil volume figure
Q091.memo: Says no attack on Iran before midterms on November 3 while blockade continues and oil flows.

Q092.memo: Links opinion piece welcoming Khamenei death.

Q093.credibility_cue: Court ruling is verifiable; mostly legal-win claim
Q093.memo: Celebrates Court of International Trade upholding end of de minimis exemption.

Q094.memo: Reports Iranian drones hit a cargo ship in Hormuz, three shot down, calls it ceasefire violation.

Q095.memo: Requests Commerce and USTR study copper imports; says tariffs will rebuild copper industry.

Q096.credibility_cue: Specific sector; reasoning tied to royal visit; no date
Q096.memo: Announces removal of tariffs and restrictions on Scotch whisky in honor of UK king and queen.

Q097.credibility_cue: Short; declares ceasefire over while talks continue
Q097.memo: States Iran requested continued talks, agreed, but ceasefire is over.

Q098.memo: Claims Iran is being destroyed, attacks NYT, promises action today.

Q099.memo: Links video of NATO chief praising Operation Epic Fury.

Q100.memo: Reports Navy disabled and seized Iranian cargo ship TOUSKA trying to run the blockade.

Q101.memo: Repeat link on Iranian opposition praise for deal.

Q102.memo: Retweets article saying peace deal with Iran eases oil prices before elections.

Q103.memo: Attacks Ontario electricity surcharge and Canadian farm tariffs, promises reciprocal tariffs on April 2.

Q104.credibility_cue: Concrete naval action effective immediately; talks failed on nuclear
Q104.memo: Announces blockade of ships entering or leaving Hormuz after talks failed on nuclear, plus interdiction of toll payers and mine clearing.

Q105.credibility_cue: Blockade stays until final deal; cites both sides
Q105.memo: Says Israel and Iran want ceasefire, final peace talks proceed, blockade continues until deal.

Q106.memo: Says talks with Iran continue at rapid pace.

Q107.memo: Says negotiators told not to rush, blockade stays until deal signed, contrasts with Obama deal, invites Abraham Accords.

Q108.credibility_cue: Duplicate of Q086; no rates or dates
Q108.memo: Repeats reciprocal tariff policy matching foreign tariffs and VAT and orders cabinet to implement.

Q109.credibility_cue: Threat with sequencing but no date
Q109.memo: Says bridges next then power plants; new regime knows what to do fast.

Q110.memo: Sets out uranium handling: turned over to US or destroyed in place with atomic agency witness.

Q111.credibility_cue: Names approving parties; signing time TBD; blockade stays
Q111.memo: Cancels strikes because talks reached top Iranian leadership and were approved; blockade stays until signing.

Q112.memo: Attacks House war powers vote as undermining final negotiations.

Q113.credibility_cue: Exact time and date for delivery
Q113.memo: Announces tariff letters or deals delivered from noon Monday July 7.

Q114.credibility_cue: Asks critics to be quiet; says Iran wants deal
Q114.memo: Says Iran really wants a deal and criticizes domestic critics for hindering negotiation.

Q115.credibility_cue: Exact date and time; ties to Iranian request
Q115.memo: Pauses energy plant destruction ten days until April 6, 8 pm ET; says talks going well.

Q116.memo: Claims Iran apologized to neighbors, then says Iran will be hit very hard today and widens targets.

Q117.credibility_cue: Demands for third parties; lengthy; not tied to dated trigger
Q117.memo: Says Gulf and other states should sign Abraham Accords alongside Iran deal; otherwise no deal; no deal means renewed fighting.

Q118.memo: Links article saying Pope commends US-Iran deal ahead of Friday signing.

Q119.credibility_cue: Responds to reported Iranian statement; no specifics
Q119.memo: Warns Iran not to hit hard or US will respond with unprecedented force.

Q120.memo: Rejects claims he is anxious to end Iran war, says time is on US side, blockade tight.

Q121.memo: Says short-term oil price rise is small cost; prices will fall once nuclear threat ends.

Q122.memo: Says Epic Fury ends and Hormuz opens to all if Iran agrees; otherwise heavier bombing.

Q123.credibility_cue: Same-day strike plus future seizure of oil sites; Venezuela analogy
Q123.memo: Announces heavy strikes tonight and eventual taking of Kharg Island and Iranian oil control.

Q124.memo: Says Iran wants deal quickly; he will decide whether US engages.

Q125.memo: Says Iran deal far better than JCPOA, recounts $1.7B cash payment, attacks critics.

Q126.credibility_cue: Conditional on oil flow stoppage; gift framing to China
Q126.memo: Warns Iran of twenty-times-harder attack if oil flow through Hormuz stops; frames protection as gift to China.

Q127.credibility_cue: Concrete fee replaced by investment pledges; reverses earlier fee
Q127.memo: Says Hormuz open to all but Iran, full blockade on Iranian trade, replaces 20% fee with Gulf investment deals.

Q128.credibility_cue: Spin on Iranian motives; claims $500M daily losses
Q128.memo: Says Iran really wants Hormuz open but blockade closed it; no deal if opened without a deal.

Q129.memo: Says tariffs will be paid starting August 1, 2025, no change, no extensions.

Q130.credibility_cue: Specific fee 20% and rename; concrete blockade restart
Q130.memo: Reinstates blockade on Iranian shipping, declares Hormuz open to others, announces 20% reimbursement fee on cargo.

Q131.memo: Attacks Senator Reed for saying deal is worse than JCPOA and calls for impeachment.

Q132.memo: Reports destruction of biggest Iranian bridge, promises more, urges Iran to make a deal.

Q133.credibility_cue: Clear rule: one bridge or power plant per ship attack
Q133.memo: Declares each Iranian attack on shipping in Hormuz will trigger destruction of one bridge or power plant.

Q134.memo: Links Newsmax article quoting Azerbaijani official that Iran deal possible.

Q135.memo: Announces secret mission moved over 100 million barrels and 200 ships through Hormuz.

Q136.credibility_cue: Reminds of past ten-day deadline; 48 hours stated
Q136.memo: Warns Iran has 48 hours to make a deal or open Hormuz before heavy attacks.

themes.description: Threats of heavy strikes paired with conditional postponements credited to mediators or Iranian requests.
Posts with dates, rates, counts and named procedures versus slogans, boasts and mood claims.

themes.theme: Hormuz as bargaining lever and fact claim
themes.description: Blockade, tolls, mines and oil volume used both as leverage and as asserted facts.
Statements on talks, blockade, fees and ceasefire change across posts, reducing reliability of any single claim.
Claims of imminent or complete deals with terms unseen, defended against critics.
Third-party links and retweets that add no own commitment.
